notes: Template-level label for every statement; parameters only for executable templates. Duplicates within a method are kept per statement and merge to one canonical key.

items.statement: Check for topological defects of the pial surface using mris_euler_number, as defects cause mris_compute_lgi to crash.
items.quote: In case of topological defects of the pial surface (run mris_euler_number), mris_compute_lgi crashes.

items.statement: T1-weighted MR scan of a macaque brain as the primary input.
items.quote: CIVET takes as input a T1w scan and registers if to standardized space, herein the NMT

items.statement: Input data must be in BIDS format, with T1w and T2w images expected.
items.quote: All the data have to be in BIDS format to run properly

items.statement: T1 weighted images are expected with the _T1w BIDS extension.
items.quote: _T1w (BIDS) extension is expected for T1 weighted images

items.statement: T2 weighted images are expected with the _T2w BIDS extension.
items.quote: _T2w (BIDS) extension is expected for T2 weighted images

items.statement: All files with the same extension (T1w or T2w) will be aligned to the first one and averaged.
items.quote: All files with the same extension (T1w or T2w) will be aligned to the first one and averaged

items.statement: The -data parameter must point to an existing BIDS format directory.
items.quote: -data : path to your data dataset (existing BIDS format directory)

items.statement: The -out parameter must point to an existing output path.
items.quote: -out : path to the output results (an existing path)

items.statement: The -soft parameter must be either SPM or ANTS, with SPM requiring a specific version of macapype/skullTo3d not available by default.
items.quote: -soft : can be one of these : SPM or ANTS ( NB: SPM requires a specific version of macapype/skullTo3d, not available by default)

items.statement: Either -params or -species must be provided; -params is mandatory if -species is omitted, and vice versa.
items.quote: -params : (mandatory if -species is omitted) a json file specifiying the global parameters of the analysis.

items.statement: The -test option can be used to check if the full pipeline is coherent, generating only graph.dot and graph.png.
items.quote: _test : (at the end) to check if the full pipeline is coherent (will only generate the graph.dot and graph.png)

items.statement: The -prep option performs only data preparation, without brain extraction and segmentation.
items.quote: _prep (at the end) will perform data preparation (no brain extraction and segmentation)

items.statement: The -noseg option performs data preparation and brain extraction, but no segmentation.
items.quote: _noseg (at the end) will perform data preparation and brain extraction (no segmentation)

items.statement: The _4animal option uses bet4animal (FSL) for brain extraction, for faster computation; by default atlas_brex is used.
items.quote: _4animal : will use bet4animal (FSL) for brain extraction, for faster computation (by default atlas_brex is used)

items.statement: The marmoT2 species option can be used for segmenting from the T2w image; by default, T1w is used for marmo.
items.quote: NB : marmoT2 can be used for segmenting from the T2w image (by default, T1w is used for marmo)

items.statement: Some templates are available in downgraded versions (e.g., baboon1_0p6, macaque_0p5) showing significant decrease in processing time with low reduction in quality, but not all combinations are available.
items.quote: NB : some templates are available in downgraded versions: baboon1_0p6, baboon2_0p6 baboon3_0p6 and macaque_0p5 and show significant decrease in processing time with low redection in quality. However, not all combinations are available

items.statement: One or more co-registered MRI volumes in Nifti (.nii/.nii.gz) or FreeSurfer (.mgz) format.
items.quote: takes one or more co-registered MRI volumes as input

items.statement: All input volumes must be co-registered with each other and have the same image grid size and voxel dimensions.
items.quote: the only requirement is that all input volumes are co-registered with each other, and have the same image grid size and voxel dimensions

items.statement: For multi-contrast data, it is recommended to select the contrast with the highest spatial resolution and reformat all other contrasts to that grid.
items.quote: it is recommended to select the contrast with the highest spatial resolution (smallest voxel size) and reformat all other contrasts to that

items.statement: For longitudinal processing, all time points must be co-registered and reformatted to the same image grid, using an unbiased reference template.
items.quote: longitudinal SAMSEG expects all its input images to have been co-registered and reformatted to the same image grid beforehand

items.statement: Preprocessing with FreeSurfer is neither required nor recommended for basic SAMSEG.
items.quote: Preprocessing of the scan(s) with FreeSurfer is neither required nor recommended

items.statement: For multi-contrast input, all volumes must be co-registered and have the same image grid size and voxel dimensions.
items.quote: all input volumes are co-registered with each other, and have the same image grid size and voxel dimensions

items.statement: For longitudinal SAMSEG, the same combination of contrasts must be provided for each time point.
items.quote: SAMSEG expects that the same combination of contrasts is provided for each time point

items.statement: When using the lesion flag, the lesion-mask-pattern is optional but strongly recommended.
items.quote: --lesion-mask-pattern <pattern> (optional but strongly recommended)

items.statement: Verify that all input volumes are co-registered and have the same image grid size and voxel dimensions.
items.quote: the only requirement is that all input volumes are co-registered with each other, and have the same image grid size and voxel dimensions

items.statement: For longitudinal processing, ensure that the same combination of contrasts is provided for each time point.
items.quote: SAMSEG expects that the same combination of contrasts is provided for each time point

items.statement: When using the lesion flag, verify that the lesion-mask-pattern has one number for each input contrast.
items.quote: The pattern is a sequence of numbers, one number for each input contrast

items.statement: The pallidum is treated internally as a white matter structure by default because it typically cannot be discerned easily from white matter in T1w scans.
items.quote: by default SAMSEG will treat the pallidum internally as a white matter structure, since it typically can't be discerned easily from white matter in T1w scans

items.statement: The first time the MS lesion module is run, the user may be prompted to install Tensorflow.
items.quote: The first time you run this module, you may be prompted to install Tensorflow

items.statement: For longitudinal processing, simply reformatting all follow-up time points to the baseline scan would introduce a longitudinal processing bias.
items.quote: simply reformatting all follow-up time points to the baseline scan would introduce a longitudinal processing bias

items.statement: Optionally a FreeSurfer .label file giving vertex indices, with optional per-vertex scalars.
items.quote: Load in a Freesurfer .label file.

items.statement: Optionally a triangular surface mesh geometry file supplying vertex coordinates and faces.
items.quote: Read a triangular format Freesurfer surface mesh.

items.statement: Verify that the number of morphometry values matches the number of vertices in the annotation.
items.quote: labelsndarray, shape (n_vertices,)

items.statement: Confirm the length of the label names list equals the number of labels in the color table.
items.quote: The names of the labels. The length of the list is n_labels.

items.statement: A FreeSurfer surface mesh file in triangular format, e.g., white or pial surface.
items.quote: Read a triangular format Freesurfer surface mesh.

items.statement: Vertex coordinates array (nvtx x 3) from the surface mesh.
items.quote: nvtx x 3 array of vertex (x, y, z) coordinates.

items.statement: Face array (nfaces x 3) defining mesh triangles.
items.quote: nfaces x 3 array of defining mesh triangles.

items.statement: Triangle vertices in (n, 3, 3) float form for area computation.
items.quote: Functions for dealing with triangle soups in (n, 3, 3) float form.

items.statement: The mesh must be in triangular format as read by nibabel's read_geometry.
items.quote: Read a triangular format Freesurfer surface mesh.

items.statement: Triangle vertices must be provided as an (n, 3, 3) float array for area calculation.
items.quote: triangles ((n, 3, 3) float) – Vertices of triangles

items.statement: The area function computes the sum area of input triangles.
items.quote: Calculates the sum area of input triangles

items.statement: Verify that the mesh is in triangular format as expected by read_geometry.
items.quote: Read a triangular format Freesurfer surface mesh.

items.statement: Ensure the triangle array is in (n, 3, 3) float form before calling area.
items.quote: triangles ((n, 3, 3) float) – Vertices of triangles

items.statement: Confirm that the area function returns the summed area, not individual triangle areas, when the sum argument is used.
items.quote: sum (bool) – Return summed area or individual triangle area

items.statement: The area function may accept precomputed cross products as a speedup, but this is optional.
items.quote: crosses ((n, 3) float or None) – As a speedup don’t re- compute cross products

items.statement: T1-weighted anatomical image(s) in DICOM or other native scanner format.
items.quote: the raw data from the scan must be converted into a format recognized by FreeSurfer

items.statement: Subject directory created via recon-all -i command.
items.quote: recon-all -i <path-to-first-structural> [-i <path-to-second-structural>] -s <subjid>

items.statement: Output volumes from recon-all processing, including T1.mgz, brainmask.mgz, and surface files.
items.quote: load the T1 and brainmask images as underlays in freeview, and overlay the white and pial surfaces

items.statement: Anatomical data should have good quality: strong contrast between tissue types, no movement, high resolution.
items.quote: If your anatomical data is of good quality - strong contrast between the tissue types, no movement, high resolution

items.statement: Soft failures occur when recon-all finishes without errors but output has obvious errors needing fixes.
items.quote: Soft Failures, on the other hand, occur when recon-all has finished without any errors - but upon closer observation of the output there are obvious errors

items.statement: Verify that surfaces follow the true boundaries of gray and white matter by visual inspection.
items.quote: Make sure that the surfaces follow the true boundaries of the top and bottom of the gray matter.

items.statement: Small and infrequent discrepancies between FreeSurfer-drawn borders and actual gray/white borders should be left alone, as editing may worsen the problem.
items.quote: as long as the discrepancies are relatively small and infrequent, it’s best to leave them alone. In those cases, sometimes editing the surfaces can make the problem worse, not better.

items.statement: White matter segmentation errors caused by lesions or gliomas are relatively uncommon in healthy subjects and are not covered in the tutorial.
items.quote: These are relatively uncommon in healthy subjects, and will not be covered in this course.

items.statement: Topological defects are very rare since FreeSurfer version 6.0 and are usually automatically fixed during recon-all.
items.quote: Since the release of FreeSurfer version 6.0 these types of errors are very rare, and they are usually automatically fixed during recon-all.

items.statement: For populations where aseg tools are ineffective (e.g., monkey or newborn data), use the -noaseg flag to skip subcortical segmentation.
items.quote: If you are working with a population for which the aseg tools will not be effective, e.g., monkey data and newborn data, use the flag -noaseg.
